description: Schur–Weyl Markov weight w_(3,1,1,1)(q) for partition λ = (3, 1, 1, 1) ⊢ 6.  Trust profile {axiom: 1, mathlib-cited: 2, derived: 1, script-cited: 0, computational: 0} — fully-trusted modulo the AXIOM (Hecke energy) and the Schur + Wedderburn first-principles entrypoints.  Generated by `build_schur_weyl_weight_general.py`; uses `schur_weyl_symbolic.partitions_of` and `schur_weyl_symbolic.hook_lengths` as the combinatorial base.

steps.name: q-integer [k]_q := (q^k − q^{-k})/(q − q^{-1})
steps.operation: Define [k]_q := (q^k − q^{-k}) / (q − q^{-1}); same definition used in every per-λ chain (the (q − q^{-1}) denominator is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale).

steps.name: Hook-length data for λ = (3, 1, 1, 1)
steps.operation: For λ = (3, 1, 1, 1) ⊢ 6, hook lengths are [6, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1] (via `schur_weyl_symbolic.hook_lengths`).  l(λ) = 4, n − l(λ) = 2.
steps.notes: Mathlib's `Mathlib.Combinatorics.Young.YoungDiagram` exposes `hookLength`; the value is read off the Young diagram combinatorially.  Source on the Python side: `folio-assistant/computations/schur_weyl_symbolic.hook_lengths`.

steps.name: Wedderburn block dimension f_λ for λ = (3, 1, 1, 1)
steps.operation: From Wedderburn, H_6(q) = ⊕_λ M_{f_λ}(K(q)) where f_λ counts standard Young tableaux of shape λ.  Hook-length formula: f_λ = n! / ∏ h_x(λ) = 10.

steps.name: Markov weight w_(3,1,1,1)(q)
steps.notes: Pure algebra: substitute the hook lengths from step 2 and the exponent (n − l(λ)) from step 2 into the convention.  The (q − q^{-1})^(n − l(λ)) prefactor arises from Hoefsmit's normalisation of the simple reps of H_n(q); it ensures the Markov stabilisation tr_M(α σ_n) = z · tr_M(α) holds with the canonical stabilisation parameter z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}).
